paper.title_en: Probing proximity-induced superconductivity in bilayer graphene using gate-defined quantum dots
paper.abstract_en: Van der Waals heterostructures enable the combination of two-dimensional (2D) materials with different electronic properties in a single device. Bilayer graphene (BLG) is particularly attractive as its electrically tunable band gap enables local control of tunnel barriers and quantum dots (QDs). Here, we realize an all-2D hybrid platform based on BLG proximitized by superconducting NbSe$_2$. Using electrostatic gates, we define tunnel barriers and QDs at different distances from the superconductor-semiconductor interface. The QDs serve as local spectroscopic probes of the proximitized BLG channel, forming tunable superconductor-quantum dot-normal conductor junctions. Coulomb blockade and finite-bias spectroscopy reveal a proximity-induced superconducting gap of up to $80\,\mathrm{μeV}$ and allow to track its evolution with distance from the NbSe$_2$ contact. The local density of states remains suppressed over distances exceeding $1\,μ$m. Our results demonstrate the potential of BLG-superconductor hybrids as a tunable platform combining QDs and quantum point contacts with superconductivity.
